experiment: H6C current incumbent versus original CC2 evaluator checkpoint
purpose: Measure cumulative strategy improvement directly against the legacy CC2 evaluator baseline after promoting H6C; this is a checkpoint, not a new parameter-selection round.

baseline.name: legacy CC2 evaluator under shared corrected mechanics
baseline.definition: Legacy Cold Clear 2 strategy/evaluator values under the same corrected S2 mechanics, information boundary, zero-gravity policy and KO arena; not a byte-for-byte upstream CC2 binary.

shared_protocol.preview: current + exactly NEXT 5; seven-bag speculation beyond visible preview

decision.reason: H6C was already promoted in its fixed-finalist confirmation. This checkpoint independently establishes a large cumulative advantage over the legacy evaluator baseline under the shared corrected S2 experiment policy.

interpretation: The sequential H1 -> H2 -> H6C gains do not merely form an incumbent ancestry chain; the current H6C policy also defeats the legacy evaluator directly on a large untouched holdout.
All ten 100-game batches favored H6C, with candidate wins ranging from 74 to 83 per batch.

This result validates the current incumbent as the base for H7 combo-interaction work; it does not imply that pending_safety=1, useful_attack_reward=1, or row_transition_scale=2.5 are individually globally optimal.
limitations: Arena is a zero-gravity alternating-lock S2 simplification rather than a wall-clock multiplayer simulator.
